story_type: spacecraft pyrotechnic jettison test, high speed camera
hook: This cover has to blow off before Orion's parachutes can open.
narration: This cover sits on top of Orion's parachutes. It has to blow off before they can open.
NASA filmed this test at four thousand frames per second, so a split second lasts half a minute.
The capsule is an Orion test article in Sandusky, Ohio, part of eleven months of testing to keep the Artemis Two crew safe.
[short pause] A catch net hung just above it, ready to catch the cover the instant it fired off.
outcome: The cover blew clear of the capsule, and NASA completed the jettison test.
title: Orion cover blown off at 4,000 fps
description:
In November 2024, NASA completed the Forward Bay Cover jettison test on an Orion test capsule at the Neil Armstrong Test Facility in Sandusky, Ohio, filmed by a high speed camera at 4,000 frames per second. The cover is the last piece that must eject right before Orion's parachutes deploy.

facts.claim: Orion test article in Sandusky, Ohio; 11-month campaign for Artemis II safety
facts.source_quote: The Orion Crew Module, also known as the Orion Environmental Test Article (ETA), returned to NASA’s Neil Armstrong Test Facility in Sandusky, Ohio, in January 2024 and completed an 11-month test campaign necessary for the safety and success of Artemis II.

facts.claim: FBC jettison test completed Nov 2024; last piece to eject before parachutes
facts.source_quote: In November 2024, experts completed the Forward Bay Cover jettison test, which is the last piece that must eject right before parachutes deploy.
This high speed video was recorded at 4,000 frames per second.
